children: Wildcat Resources
has established a maiden Inferred mineral resource of 14.8 million tonnes at 1.0% lithium oxide (Li₂O) at its Bolt Cutter Central project in Western Australia’s Pilbara region.
Reported at a 0.7% Li₂O cut-off grade, the estimate lifts its combined lithium resources with the nearby Tabba Tabba project by about 20% to 88.3Mt at 1.0% Li₂O.
Bolt Cutter Central—which is located 10 kilometres west of Tabba Tabba—is being assessed as a possible source of supplementary material for the proposed processing operation.
Wildcat has begun studies into that option following early laboratory results that indicated the deposits may be able to use a common processing approach.
Harry and Hermione Swarms
The resource covers the Harry and Hermione pegmatite swarms, where mineralisation reaches the surface and the principal Harry zone is locally thickest at shallow depths.
About 90% of the Inferred resource is within 160 metres of surface, prompting consideration of open-pit mining as part of future technical studies.
The mineralised system remains open along strike and at depth, with further targets identified beyond the resource boundary and between established mineralised zones.
At a lower 0.6% Li₂O cut-off, Bolt Cutter Central would contain 20.4Mt at 0.9% Li₂O, and Wildcat plans to test extensions to known pegmatites and additional prospects.
Wildcat will also examine mining economics, haulage and available plant capacity before determining whether a satellite operation could contribute to the broader development.
Drill-Core Samples
Initial testing of three drill-core samples through the processing method developed for Tabba Tabba achieved average laboratory lithium recovery of 82.5% and a concentrate grade of 5.66% Li₂O.
Those results provide an early basis for examining whether material from Bolt Cutter Central could be treated at the planned Tabba Tabba plant rather than requiring a separate facility.

“Encouraging initial metallurgical results using the flowsheet developed for Tabba Tabba also provide a foundation for investigating Bolt Cutter Central as a source of supplementary feed,” managing director AJ Saverimutto said.
“Our focus is to rapidly advance these assessments and test opportunities for further resource growth.”

Geology manager Torrin Rowe said the work had “strengthened our understanding of the controls on mineralisation and provides a foundation for testing extensions to the known pegmatites and exploring additional compelling targets across our extensive Pilbara landholding.”
Tabba Tabba Studies
The October 2026 definitive feasibility study for Tabba Tabba envisaged staged processing capacity rising from 2.25Mt a year to 4.5Mt a year.
Based on a Probable Ore Reserve of 48.3Mt at 0.97% Li₂O, that development case does not incorporate Bolt Cutter Central in its production schedule or financial forecasts.
Accordingly, the new Inferred resource is not an addition to the project’s Ore Reserve and any production contribution will depend on more detailed evaluation and approvals.
Planned work includes a scoping study, environmental baseline assessments, further metallurgical testing, and an application for a mining lease over Bolt Cutter Central.
Wildcat held $76.1 million in cash at 30 September 2026 as it prepares to investigate those options and continue exploration across its Pilbara tenements.

title: Wildcat Resources Adds to Lithium Portfolio with Maiden Bolt Cutter Central Resource
